messages:
From: Anna Cole <anna@kitebridge.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: POC environment requirements for KiteBridge MAP

Hey Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency numbers. We've kicked the internal review forward and would like to lock the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to get a POC running next month. To scope the MAP, can you confirm what you need from us for the environment setup? Specifically: API keys and org setup, IP allowlist (we run behind a small egress range), and VPC peering for the staging tenant.

I've attached an initial draft of our goals and timeline (KB-MAP-v1.pdf). Our InfraOps lead (infra@kitebridge.com) will be the technical owner.

High level asks from us:
- A short checklist of what Redwood needs to provision (API key shape, service account, org ID).
- Target windows for VPC peering (we have a maintenance window Tue/Wed 03:00-06:00 UTC preferred).
- Any ephemeral key cadence for security reviews.

Can you send a proposed MAP with milestone dates? We're aiming for a 3-week POC: week 0 provisioning, week 1 smoke tests, week 2 performance soak and final evaluation.

Thanks,
Anna Cole
Head of Product
KiteBridge

Attachments: KB-MAP-v1.pdf (PDF, 320KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: POC environment requirements for KiteBridge MAP

Hi Anna — appreciate the clear list. Looping in Neha (onboarding eng) and Marissa (CS lead) so we can convert the draft into a concrete MAP with milestone owners.

Short answers up-front:
- API keys/org: we'll create a scoped service API key for the staging tenant and provide a short-lived bootstrap token for the initial sync. We need KiteBridge's org display name and desired tenant ID (can be a short string).
- IP allowlist: please send the small egress CIDR list (or the .csv format). We will publish a publishable endpoint and add those CIDRs to the staging tenant firewall.
- VPC peering: Redwood supports AWS VPC peering and Transit Gateway. For a standard peering we need the VPC ID, account ID, and preferred peering window. Tue/Wed 03:00-06:00 UTC works for us.

I'll attach a one-page network allowlist template for your Infra team to fill and return. Once Neha confirms timing, we'll propose exact milestone dates.

Proposed high-level MAP (we'll formalize in HubSpot):
- Day 0–2: org + tenant creation, API key issuance, access review (owner: Redwood - Neha)
- Day 3–5: VPC peering + IP allowlist applied (owner: KiteBridge Infra + Redwood network eng)
- Day 6–10: smoke tests and API validation (owner: KiteBridge SRE + Redwood CS)
- Day 11–15: soak tests and performance evaluation (owner: KiteBridge Product + Redwood PM)

I'll ask Neha to send a technical checklist and to confirm the peering runbook. Attaching: kitebridge-network-allowlist.csv (template).

—Karthik
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kitebridge-network-allowlist.csv (CSV template)

Hi Anna — Neha here. Below is the technical checklist and suggested timeline we use for MAP-driven POCs. Sharing so KiteBridge Infra can fill the items in bold.

Tech checklist (action items)
1) Org & tenant
   - Provide desired tenant ID (short string) — ACTION: KiteBridge
   - Required contact (platform SRE): full name + email — ACTION: KiteBridge
2) API keys & bootstrap
   - We will issue: one long-lived service key scoped to staging (rotatable) + one short-lived bootstrap token (TTL default 8h, can set to 24h on request) — ACTION: Redwood (Neha)
   - Provide any existing IP allowlist for management console access if you have tighter controls — ACTION: KiteBridge
3) IP allowlist
   - Fill and return the attached CSV (we accept a max of 50 CIDRs for staging).
   - If your egress is behind NAT, please include the public NAT IPs. — ACTION: KiteBridge
4) VPC peering
   - Confirm VPC ID, account ID, and desired peering window. We will create a peering request and schedule the acceptance step during the maintenance window. Preferred acceptance: Tue/Wed 03:00–06:00 UTC. — ACTION: KiteBridge + Redwood Network
5) Security/compliance
   - If you require ephemeral key rotation cadence > 24h, let us know; SOC2 customers commonly ask for 8–24h bootstrap TTL.
6) Smoke & soak tests (sample checks)
   - Token auth, seed prompt latencies, KV cache hit verification, prefix caching validation — ACTION: joint runbook

Suggested MAP dates (if we start provisioning Monday, May 25):
- May 25–26: tenant + API key issuance (owner: Redwood)
- May 27–28: VPC peering + allowlist apply (owner: joint)
- May 29–31: smoke tests and functional sign-off (owner: KiteBridge + Redwood)
- Jun 1–4: soak/perf evaluation and scorecard (owner: KiteBridge product + Redwood PM)

Operational notes:
- Billing for the POC can be charged to your eval card; we can invoice if procurement requests it.
- We will provide a per-route token breakdown via the Console by default; we'll also export a CSV on request.

Next steps: KiteBridge Infra to return the filled CSV and confirm Maya R. as the peering contact. Once received we'll raise the peering request and post the runbook in HubSpot (link to be added).

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Onboarding Engineer
Redwood Inference
